subject: Numeracy
title: Our maths celebration
objectives: Children will show Year learning through games and stations.
Teachers will complete every child’s end-of-year record and transition note.
content: Revising the year’s numeracy learning through games and stations, celebrating achievements and completing each child’s end-of-year record.
teachingActivities: Keep the week relaxed and celebratory; observe quietly; record evidence; prepare a transition note for the next class.
learnerActivities: Play favourite maths games, show what they know, celebrate with friends and share their learning with families.
assessment: Use the three term records and this week’s evidence to complete the end-of-year record for every strand: sorting and matching, comparing and measuring, number and counting, shape and space, pattern and time, and mathematical language. Record Secure only with evidence from two or more occasions.
expectedOutcomes: Takes part confidently in familiar maths games.
Each child has an end-of-year observation record.
crossCurricular: Literacy: songs and rhymes from the year
Social Habits: celebrating together and thanking friends

lessons.title: Counting and number games
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit counting to five, one more and sharing through games.
successCriteria: Counts up to five objects by touching
Adds one more or shares one each
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met counting to five, numerals, measures, patterns, shapes, position, time, one more and sharing during the year.
lessons.starter: Beat the drum five times and say "One, two, three, four, five." Say "Today we play our favourite counting games."
teacherActivities: Play "Count the blocks" with a tray of up to five blocks.
Play "One more" with fruits and ask "How many now?"
Play "One for you, one for me" with toys and plates.
Match numeral cards to groups of objects.
learnerActivities: Children touch and count the blocks.
Children add one more and say the new number.
Children share one each with friends.
Children match numerals to groups with support.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play "Count the blocks" with a tray of up to five blocks. Children: Children touch and count the blocks.
Step 2. Teacher: Play "One more" with fruits and ask "How many now?" Children: Children add one more and say the new number.
Step 3. Teacher: Play "One for you, one for me" with toys and plates. Children: Children share one each with friends.
Step 4. Teacher: Match numeral cards to groups of objects. Children: Children match numerals to groups with support.

practical.title: Number game stations
steps: Set up stations for counting, one more and sharing.
practical.safety: Use large toy items only; supervise stations; keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Count only to three and play with an adult partner.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count to five and tell a friend how many.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many blocks?
questions.expected: The correct number up to five.

expectedOutcomes: Counts, adds one more and shares
lessons.conclusion: Sing a counting song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Count and share at home with a family member.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit counting to five, one more and sharing through games" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Shape, size and position games
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit shapes, comparing size and position through games.
successCriteria: Names or points to circle, square and triangle
Uses a comparison or position word
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met counting to five, numerals, measures, patterns, shapes, position, time, one more and sharing during the year.
lessons.starter: Say "Show me a circle! Show me a long rope! Go behind the chair!" Say "Today we play games about shapes and size."
teacherActivities: Play shape hunt: find a circle, a square and a triangle.
Compare long and short ropes and heavy and light baskets.
Play position games with the chair and tunnel.
Ask the children to tell a friend one thing they can do.
learnerActivities: Children find and name shapes.
Children choose the longer rope and heavier basket.
Children follow instructions and say position words.
Child shows or says one skill.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Play shape hunt: find a circle, a square and a triangle. Children: Children find and name shapes.
Step 2. Teacher: Compare long and short ropes and heavy and light baskets. Children: Children choose the longer rope and heavier basket.
Step 3. Teacher: Play position games with the chair and tunnel. Children: Children follow instructions and say position words.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask the children to tell a friend one thing they can do. Children: Child shows or says one skill.

practical.title: Shape and position circuit
steps: Set up a shape hunt, a measure station and a position course.
Children visit each with a friend.
practical.safety: Use low equipment; supervise stations; keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Do one activity at a time with an adult.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to teach a friend a game.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Names shapes and uses position words
lessons.conclusion: Sing the position song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Play shape and position games at home.

lessons.title: Full, empty, morning and night
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will revisit capacity and time words through play.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met counting to five, numerals, measures, patterns, shapes, position, time, one more and sharing during the year.
resources: Cups and a basin of water
lessons.starter: Show a full cup and an empty cup. Say "Full! Empty!" Show the sun and the moon and say "Day! Night!"
teacherActivities: Pour water into cups and ask "Full or empty?"
Sort day and night picture cards under the sun and the moon.
Put the cards of the school day in order.
Ask "What do we do in the morning?" and "What do we do at night?"
learnerActivities: Children pour and say the word.
Children sort cards and say "day" or "night".
Children place the cards in order with help.
Children answer with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Pour water into cups and ask "Full or empty?" Children: Children pour and say the word.
Step 2. Teacher: Sort day and night picture cards under the sun and the moon. Children: Children sort cards and say "day" or "night".
Step 3. Teacher: Put the cards of the school day in order. Children: Children place the cards in order with help.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What do we do in the morning?" and "What do we do at night?" Children: Children answer with a word or action.

practical.title: Water and time stations
steps: Set up a water station and a time sorting station.
practical.safety: Supervise water play; wipe spills at once; wash hands after.

differentiation.support: Use full and empty only, with an adult partner.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to tell the story of their day in order.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Is the cup full or empty?

lessons.conclusion: Sing the day song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about the parts of the day at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "revisit capacity and time words through play" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Our maths party
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will use number, shape and sharing words in a pretend party.
successCriteria: Uses shape or number words in play
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met counting to five, numerals, measures, patterns, shapes, position, time, one more and sharing during the year.
lessons.starter: Spread the party cloth and say "Our toys are having a maths party. Who can set the table for four guests?"
teacherActivities: Ask children to put one plate and one cup for each guest.
Ask "Can you find a round plate and a square tray?"
Ask children to share five biscuits among the guests.
Sing a party song with a clapping pattern.
learnerActivities: Children place one plate and one cup at each place.
Children find shapes at the party table.
Children share and count what is left.
Children clap in a pattern and sing.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Ask children to put one plate and one cup for each guest. Children: Children place one plate and one cup at each place.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Can you find a round plate and a square tray?" Children: Children find shapes at the party table.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask children to share five biscuits among the guests. Children: Children share and count what is left.
Step 4. Teacher: Sing a party song with a clapping pattern. Children: Children clap in a pattern and sing.

practical.title: Maths party table
steps: Set the table with one plate and cup for each guest.
practical.safety: Use toy items; supervise role play; wash hands after play.

differentiation.support: Set the table for two guests only.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to set the table for five guests and say how many plates.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How many plates for four guests?

expectedOutcomes: Uses number and shape words in play
lessons.conclusion: Say thank you to the guests and tidy the party table together.
lessons.homeConnection: Help to set the table at home and count the plates.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "use number, shape and sharing words in a pretend party" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Show and celebrate our year
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show their year of numeracy learning in familiar games and celebrate their work.
successCriteria: Takes part confidently in at least three familiar tasks
Shows or says one thing they have learned this year
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have met counting to five, numerals, measures, patterns, shapes, position, time, one more and sharing during the year.
lessons.starter: Play a favourite song from the year. Say "Today we show what we know and celebrate how much we have learned this year."
teacherActivities: Set up six quick stations: sorting, comparing, counting, shapes, position and one more. Spend three minutes at each.
At each station ask a simple question and wait.
Take photographs of each child at work and record levels against the three-term record.
Give each child a certificate or sticker and say one thing they did well this year.
learnerActivities: Children visit stations in pairs.
Child answers or shows the response.
Children continue playing.
Children receive their award and clap for friends.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up six quick stations: sorting, comparing, counting, shapes, position and one more. Spend three minutes at each. Children: Children visit stations in pairs.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask a simple question and wait. Children: Child answers or shows the response.
Step 3. Teacher: Take photographs of each child at work and record levels against the three-term record. Children: Children continue playing.
Step 4. Teacher: Give each child a certificate or sticker and say one thing they did well this year. Children: Children receive their award and clap for friends.

practical.title: Year celebration stations
steps: Children visit each with a friend.
Teacher records evidence and takes photos.
practical.safety: Remove small items; supervise all stations; never compare children aloud.

differentiation.support: Visit three stations with an adult partner at each.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to be a station helper.

assessment.method: Observe each child at the six stations and complete the end-of-year record. Record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for each strand: sorting and matching, comparing and measuring, number and counting, shape and space, pattern and time, and mathematical language and reasoning. Write one transition sentence for the Nursery 1 teacher.

questions.question: How many blocks?
questions.expected: The correct number up to five.

lessons.conclusion: Clap for the whole class and sing the closing song. Send the end-of-year note home.
lessons.homeConnection: Parents receive an end-of-year note with strengths, next steps and home ideas for the holiday.
